s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of systemic illness with fever, diarrhea, and skin lesions
key_facts: 55-year-old woman
History of diverticulosis and colonic polyps
Low-grade fever
Facial lesions initially presented as ill-defined pink patches
Lesions spread to chest, abdomen, back, and left buttock
Mild leukocytosis with normal differential
Mildly elevated transaminase and alkaline phosphatase levels
Negative wound culture
Negative PCR for herpes simplex virus
Negative direct fluorescent antibody assay for varicella-zoster virus
Intradermal neutrophilic inflammation with ulceration on forehead lesion biopsy
Septal panniculitis with Miescher radial granulomas on right thigh biopsy
Moderate inflammation, edema, erosions, and pseudopolyps in the sigmoid colon on colonoscopy

differentials: Pyogenic sterile arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne syndrome
per_call: Pyogenic sterile arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne syndrome

shortlist.label: Sweet syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of fever, diarrhea, and skin lesions with intradermal neutrophilic inflammation

shortlist.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Skin lesions with ulceration and intracorneal neutrophils, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum

shortlist.label: Neutrophilic dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Facial lesions with intradermal neutrophilic inflammation and ulceration

shortlist.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of diverticulosis and colonic polyps, with moderate inflammation and edema in the sigmoid colon

shortlist.label: Bowel-associated dermatosis-arthritis syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Combination of gastrointestinal symptoms and skin lesions, suggesting a bowel-associated dermatosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of new-onset flulike symptoms, low-grade fever, facial crusted plaques, and bloody diarrhea, along with laboratory findings of mild leukocytosis and intradermal neutrophilic inflammation on biopsy, are consistent with Sweet syndrome, a condition characterized by neutrophilic dermatosis and often associated with underlying inflammatory bowel disease or other systemic conditions.

rejected.label: Pyoderma gangrenosum
rejected.why: While pyoderma gangrenosum can present with similar skin lesions, the absence of characteristic ulcerative lesions and the presence of intradermal neutrophilic inflammation on biopsy make Sweet syndrome a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Neutrophilic dermatosis
rejected.why: Neutrophilic dermatosis is a broader term that encompasses Sweet syndrome, but the specific clinical and laboratory findings in this case are more consistent with Sweet syndrome.

rejected.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of diverticulosis and colonic polyps, and colonoscopy showed moderate inflammation, the primary presentation is dermatologic, making Sweet syndrome a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Bowel-associated dermatosis-arthritis syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by a combination of bowel disease and dermatologic or arthritic manifestations, but the specific findings in this case are more consistent with Sweet syndrome.
